chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Church.
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly institutional, constructed to justify the alms-giving system and the catechumen-elect relationship. Teaching purity is near zero (0.023). The compiler builds a three-tier analogy: earth→tree parallels catechumens→church parallels soul→luminaries→land of light. Only ¶7-8 contain cosmological content where both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system (soul ascending through sun/moon to land of light). These may preserve fragments of older cosmological teaching about the soul's ascent, but they are embedded within and deployed in service of the institutional argument. The distinctive phrases 'house of its people' and 'country of the household' in ¶7 suggest possible preservation rather than free editorial composition. All other paragraphs are institutional or editorial. No substrate vocabulary was detected by the NLP pipeline except a trace in ¶9.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic opening: 'Once again... the enlightener sat... He says to his disciples.' No cosmological content. Standard compilation-era framing.

Entirely institutional: alms, sects, catechumens, holy church, commandments of alms. The vocabulary is saturated with church organization terms. 'Every sect overall uses his name' — polemic against rival religious communities. Seam flag confirms editorial extension. No cosmological mapping present.

'The holy church exists in two forms: in the brothers and the sisters' — institutional description of church structure. 'Alms reach the holy church, shall be redeemed through it and purified' — institutional soteriology. The 'Now' opening marks editorial continuation. Institutional score 25.49 is the highest in the chapter.

Continues institutional argument: church as 'place of rest' for alms, church depending on catechumens. 'Doorway and conveyance to that land of rest' — institutional soteriology using spatial metaphors. Seam flag fires. Institutional score 26.19, highest in chapter.

Parable of gardener/tree/earth used to illustrate catechumen-elect relationship. While the imagery (gardener, good tree, good earth, tree of life) uses organic correspondences, the framing question 'What does the assembly of catechumens resemble?' explicitly identifies the parable as institutional analogy. The parable was composed or adapted for this institutional context. Note: 'tree of life' is an ancient image, but here serves institutional illustration.

Explicit application of the ¶5 parable: 'the holy church... is like a good tree,' 'the assembly of the catechumens is like this good earth.' The decoder ring for the parable. Every sentence maps parable→institution. Institutional score 17.48.

paragraphs.core_text: This [liv]ing sou[l] that is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow[s a]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [ ... ] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the light-givers of the heavens [ ... / ... ] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Likewise' (editorial connector linking this cosmological fragment to the preceding institutional parable) and 'today' from 'that today is set in mixture' (editorial temporal marker anchoring to the present age).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: living soul → mixture → powers as obstruction → sun/moon as door → country of the household. The phrases 'house of its people' and 'country of the household of its people' are distinctive and may reflect older tradition. However, the paragraph is deployed as analogy for the catechumen-church relationship, and 'Likewise' explicitly frames it as such. The cosmological CONTENT may be substrate; its DEPLOYMENT here is editorial. Significant uncertainty about whether this preserves an older formulation or is editorial composition using standard cosmological knowledge.

paragraphs.core_text: The light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the lan[d] of light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Again, further in, also' — editorial connector serving the analogy escalation (soul→sun/moon→land of light paralleling catechumens→church→land of light).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the cosmic hierarchy from ¶7: as the soul finds rest in the luminaries, the luminaries find rest in the land of light. Both sides remain within the cosmic system. The teaching that sun and moon are intermediate vessels whose own origin/rest is the land of light is systematic cosmological knowledge. Brief and formulaic enough that it could be either preserved substrate or editorial summary.

'So, thus' marks this as editorial summary recapitulating ¶7. The content (soul purified, door opens to house of its people) repeats ¶7 in compressed form. Despite the only substrate score in the chapter (6.9), this reads as an editorial pivot — it summarizes the cosmological teaching before the chapter returns to institutional application in ¶10-11.

'Also, it is the case that' — editorial connector. The content (land of light as final receiver for light-givers, they rest and rule therein) essentially restates ¶8. This is a recapitulation that prepares for the institutional application in ¶11. The two-step summary (¶9 recaps ¶7, ¶10 recaps ¶8) is editorial structuring before the chapter's conclusion.

Closes the analogy chain: 'the holy church shall become the place of rest for the alms of the catechumens; and the catechumens themselves become the place of rest for the holy church.' Then: 'both the former and the latter, the place of rest... is the land of light.' This is the institutional application that the entire chapter was building toward. The three-tier analogy is complete: catechumens↔church↔land of light. Institutional score 23.64 confirms. Seam flag fires.
